passages.heading: Debt note
passages.text: NOTE 9 – Long-Term Debt Credit Agreement On January 23, 2026, the Company entered into a Senior Revolving Credit Agreement (the "2026 Credit Agreement") by and among the Company, certain subsidiaries of the Company party thereto, the lenders party thereto, and Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as administrative agent. The 2026 Credit Agreement provides for an unsecured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of up to $ 1,250 million, including subfacilities for standby letters of credit and swingline loans. The 2026 Credit Agreement matures on January 23, 2031 . The 2026 Credit Agreement replaced the previous secured credit facility under the credit agreement dated December 21, 2021 by and among the Company, certain subsidiaries of the Company party thereto, the lenders party thereto, and Bank of America, N.A., as the administrative agent (the “Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement”), which was scheduled to mature on December 21, 2026. Borrowings under the 2026 Credit Agreement bear interest based on the Company’s option, either (1) the applicable fixed rate plus 0.75 % to 1.125 % or (2) the daily rate plus 0.0 % to 0.125 %, in each case, depending on the Company’s consolidated total net leverage ratio. Additionally, the unused revolving commitments under the 2026 Credit Agreement are subject to the payment of a customary commitment fee at a range of 0.05 % to 0.125 %, depending on the Company’s consolidated total net leverage ratio. As of July 31, 2026, the Company had outstanding letters of credit of $ 22.5 million and the unused capacity of $ 1,227.5 million was available to us. The 2026 Credit Agreement contains representations and warranties, conditions, and covenants. As of July 31, 2026, the Company was in compliance with these financial covenants. In connection with entering into the 2026 Credit Agreement, the Company incurred $ 1.5 million in costs, which were capitalized as debt issuance fees. The debt issuance cost is amortized to interest expense over the term of the debt instrument and is included in other assets on the consolidated balance sheet.

passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should consider carefully the risks and uncertainties described below before making an investment decision. Our business could be harmed if any of these risks, as well as other risks not currently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial, materialize. The trading price of our common stock could decline due to the occurrence of any of these risks, and you may lose all or part of your investment. In assessing the risks described below, you should also refer to the other information contained in this Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and the related notes and schedules, and other filings with the SEC. Risks Related to Our Business and Industry We depend on a limited number of major vehicle sellers for a substantial portion of our revenues. The loss of one or more of these major sellers could adversely affect our consolidated results of operations and financial position, and an inability to increase our sources of vehicle supply could adversely affect our growth rates. Although no single customer accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated revenues for fiscal 2026, 2025, or 2024, a limited number of vehicle sellers historically have collectively accounted for a substantial portion of our revenues. Certain of our arrangements with vehicle sellers are non-exclusive and may be terminated or modified by the seller on limited notice or without cause, in each case subject to the terms of the applicable agreement. Vehicle sellers have terminated agreements with us in the past in particular markets, which has affected revenues in those markets. There can be no assurance that our existing agreements will not be canceled. Furthermore, there can be no assurance that we will be able to enter into future agreements with vehicle sellers or that we will be able to retain our existing supply of salvage vehicles. A reduction in vehicles from a significant vehicle seller or any material changes in the terms of an arrangement with a significant vehicle seller could have a material adverse effect on our consolidated results of operations and financial position. In addition, a failure to increase our sources of vehicle supply could adversely affect our earnings and revenue growth rates. Our expansion into markets outside the U.S., including expansions in the U.K., Canada, Europe, Brazil, and the Middle East expose us to risks arising from operating in international markets. Any failure to successfully integrate businesses acquired or operational capabilities established outside the U.S. could have an adverse effect on our consolidated results of operations, financial position, or cash flows. We first expanded our operations outside the U.S. in fiscal 2003 with an acquisition in Canada. Subsequently, in fiscal 2007 and fiscal 2008 we made significant acquisitions in the U.K., followed by acquisitions in the U.A.E., Brazil, Germany, and Spain in fiscal 2013, expansions into Bahrain and Oman in fiscal 2015, expansion into the Republic of Ireland and India in fiscal 2016, an acquisition in Finland in fiscal 2018, and an acquisition of a parts recycler in the U.K. in fi

credit_strengths.text: Copart's operating margin sits far above the consumer discretionary sector median, reflecting an auction and vehicle remarketing model with high incremental margins and limited direct cost of goods. This structural profitability supports internal cash generation and cushions earnings against volume or pricing shocks, in our view.

Liquidity is a core strength: the current ratio is exceptionally high versus the sector median, and cash balances plus unused revolver capacity provide substantial funding flexibility. We view this as ample headroom to absorb working capital swings or bolt-on acquisitions without external financing.

key_risks.text: The risk factors disclose dependence on a limited number of major vehicle sellers, with arrangements often non-exclusive and terminable on limited notice. Loss or renegotiation of a significant seller could pressure volumes and revenue growth, a concentration risk we consider material despite no single customer exceeding the disclosure threshold.

The debt note shows the new unsecured revolver matures in the medium term and replaced a secured facility, with pricing tied to consolidated net leverage. No funded borrowings were tagged at year-end, so reported leverage metrics are unavailable; we treat this as a data gap rather than evidence of zero debt.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is extraordinarily high relative to the sector median, and cash interest paid is minimal against operating income. Even allowing for capitalized interest and fees excluded from the cash proxy, debt service burden appears negligible, in our judgement, provided earnings remain near current levels.

Operating cash flow comfortably funds capital expenditure, leaving strong free cash flow, though share repurchases absorb most of it. We view internal cash generation as more than sufficient to service any revolver draw, with the main sensitivity being a sustained earnings decline rather than refinancing risk.

overall_credit_view.text: Copart presents a high-margin, cash-generative credit profile with exceptional liquidity and minimal observed debt service burden. The absence of tagged borrowings and a complete debt maturity schedule limits our leverage assessment, so we base the view on cash flow, coverage and revolver capacity rather than a computed leverage ratio.

Forward-looking, we expect stable to modestly growing revenue and continued strong free cash flow, but note shareholder distributions consume most of it, limiting deleveraging capacity if debt is drawn. Seller concentration and international expansion execution are the key watch items; overall we assess the credit as strong, subject to confirming funded debt.

credit_strengths.text: Copart的營業利潤率遠高於非必需消費品行業中位數，反映其拍賣及車輛再營銷模式具有高增量利潤率及有限直接銷售成本。我們認為，此結構性盈利能力支持內部現金生成，並在銷量或定價衝擊下緩衝盈利。
流動性是一項核心優勢：流動比率相對於行業中位數異常高，而現金結餘加上未使用的循環信貸額度提供顯著的資金靈活性。我們認為這為吸收營運資金波動或補強型收購提供了充足空間，無需外部融資。

key_risks.text: 風險因素披露依賴少數主要車輛賣家，相關安排通常非獨家且可在有限通知下終止。失去或重新談判重要賣家可能對銷量及收入增長構成壓力，我們認為此集中風險屬重大，儘管並無單一客戶超過披露門檻。
債務附註顯示新的無抵押循環信貸於中期到期，並取代了有抵押融資，定價與合併淨槓桿掛鈎。年末並無已提取借款被標記，因此報告的槓桿指標無法獲得；我們將此視為數據缺口，而非零債務的證據。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率相對於行業中位數異常高，而已付現金利息相對於營業收入極少。即使計入資本化利息及現金代理指標中排除的費用，我們判斷債務償付負擔似乎微不足道，前提是盈利維持在當前水平附近。
經營現金流輕鬆覆蓋資本支出，留下強勁的自由現金流，儘管股份回購吸收了大部分。我們認為內部現金生成足以償付任何循環信貸提取，主要敏感因素是可持續的盈利下降而非再融資風險。

overall_credit_view.text: Copart呈現高利潤率、現金生成能力強的信用狀況，具有卓越的流動性及極少的觀察到的債務償付負擔。缺乏已標記借款及完整的債務到期時間表限制了我們的槓桿評估，因此我們基於現金流、覆蓋率及循環信貸額度而非計算的槓桿比率來形成觀點。
展望未來，我們預期收入穩定至溫和增長，自由現金流持續強勁，但注意到股東分派消耗了大部分，若債務被提取則限制了去槓桿能力。賣家集中度及國際擴張執行是關鍵觀察事項；總體而言，我們評估該信用為強勁，惟須確認已融資債務。
